High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Appellant stands convicted vide judgment dated 13.03.2024 passed by learned Special Judge
(Pocso Act) Betul, District Betul in S.C. No.52/2021 for offence under Sections 363 of Ipc, 354 of
Ipc r/w Sec. 3(2)(Va) of Sc/St Act, 3/4 of Pocso Act including 376(3) of Ipc, 3(2)(v) of Sc/St Act
(including Section 3(1)(b)(i) (ii) of Sc/St Act) and sentenced to undergo Ri for three years with fine
Rs.2,000/-, Ri for three years with fine Rs.2,000/-, Imprisonment for 20 years with fine
Rs.5,000/-, Imprisonment for life with fine Rs.5,000/- for respective offences with default
stipulations.
Prosecution story found to be proved is that

on 11.09.2021, at around 1.00 A.M., when the
prosecutrix was sleeping alongwith her mother in the old house, and her father and other sibling
were sleeping in the new house, the appellant knocked the door of the house and when the
prosecutrix came outside the house, he took her near the riverside where he committed the offence.
2 Cra-4931-2024
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is not proved since no scholar register was produced during the trial, however, a certificate issued by the Panchayat in the year 2021 was produced and the trial Court relying on the same, convicted the appellant under the provisions of POCSO Act.
No injuries on the private part of the prosecutrix were found.
Even the FSL report is negative and DNA has not been conducted.

The statement of mother of the prosecutrix (PW/1) clearly shows that at the time of admission of the prosecutrix, some other date of birth was registered in the school; whereas during the trial, the certificate issued in the year Manish Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11506202/
1 2021 has been produced which clearly goes to show that the age of the prosecutrix is not established.

entities.text: Manish Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the appeal is of the year 2024, final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future and the appellant has suffered about three and half years of incarceration, therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence may be suspended and appellant may be released on bail.
Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State supported the impugned judgment and prays for rejection of application for suspension of sentence.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Having considered the rival submissions, the statement of mother of the prosecutrix (PW/1), the period of custody as also the fact that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, therefore, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A. No.31787/2024 is 3 CRA-4931-2024 allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if already not deposited, the substantive jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended till the final disposal of the appeal and he be released on bail, on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court, for his appearance before the concerned trial Court firstly on 24.06.2025 , and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the said Court in this regard.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(ANURADHA  JUDGE JUD  ak Manish Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11506202/
